title: Praxis Logistics - deep dive integration call notes
content:
Meeting: Praxis Logistics deep-dive (initial integration planning)
Date: 2025-11-06
Attendees: Leah (RW), Omar (RW SE), Rina (RW Solutions), Tom Baxter (Praxis infra lead), Mei Lin (Praxis ML), Javier Ruiz (Praxis security)

High-level ask (Praxis):
- Replace heuristic routing and manual dispatch with a low-latency inference layer for ticket classification and ETA generation.
- Hard constraints: 99th pct latency < 120ms for classification path (single-turn), sustained 200 QPS for peak minutes, data never leaves company network for classification-only pipeline.
- Secondary: longer-context summarization of routing conversations (up to 3k tokens) can be batched and handled on Dedicated or Hosted depending on residency policies.

Current infra (Praxis):
- On-prem colo with 8x NVIDIA A30 nodes behind an EKS-like k8s control plane (they run VMware + k8s).
- Strict egress: only allowed outbound to specific partner IPs via corporate proxy; no general internet access from worker nodes.
- KMS: HashiCorp Vault (transit) for keys, HSM-backed for rotation.

Key constraints / gotchas surfaced in call:
- Network egress policy will block Redwood Private from calling our hosted control plane unless we provide a whitelistable IP range or put control plane in Praxis VPC.
- MTU and jumbo frame mismatch with NVMe-backed hosts caused token streaming stalls in prior infra — Mei asked about streaming robustness when MTU < 1500.
- Their ops team is conservative on container images: must pass static SBOM / SCA gates, and only allow images signed by Praxis registry.
- Throttling during busy dispatch windows is higher risk than expected: scenarios where bursts of 2k short classification requests happen for 10–20s. Need graceful degradation.

Preliminary architecture options discussed:
1) Redwood Private (hybrid) control plane in Praxis-managed VPC with private agent in colo cluster. Pros: meets data residency, integrates with Vault. Cons: requires network plumbing + firewall updates.
2) Fully on-prem Redwood bundle (air-gapped) with local control plane. Pros: minimal egress. Cons: heavier ops, slower feature rollout.
3) Hosted API + dedicated burst gateway: classification requests proxied through an approved egress gateway and NAT pool. Pros: fastest to launch; Cons: probably fails the "data never leaves" bar for legal.

Performance notes / discussed tuning levers:
- Throughput target: 200 QPS sustained, 2k QPS burstable for 15–30s. Aim for 95th/99th token-level batching windows < 30ms.
- Model selection: recommend a trimmed classification model quantized to int8 or q8_0 to hit latency. Suggest baseline test on A30 with nvfuser kernels.
- Autoscaling: prefer policy-based CPU/GPU scaling on queue length + prefix-cache warmup. Use warm pools to handle bursts.
- Caching: prefix cache (common utterances) will likely eliminate ~40% of classification token cost. We need to capture token distribution from Praxis logs.

Prompt & routing examples captured (quick sketches):
- classification prompt (single-turn): "SYSTEM: You are the Praxis ticket classifier. Classify into: [delivery-delay, route-change, incident, pricing, other]. Return only label token."
- summarization example: "Summarize the conversation history into 3 action items, 40 tokens each." (used for longer-context path)

Security / compliance notes:
- Vault integration: they require Redwood to support Vault transit + HSM wrapping. We indicated Redwood Private supports customer KMS via PKCS11 and custom KMS endpoints.
- Auditing: Praxis asked for per-request provenance logs stored for 1 year. Redwood console can export token-level traces but will need S3-compatible endpoint in their VPC.
- Image policy: we discussed signed images + SBOM ingestion; action: capture our SBOM and signing process for their review.

Open questions (needs follow-up):
- Can Praxis open a small set of outbound IPs for the Redwood control plane, or do they require fully air-gapped? (Owner: Tom to confirm by 2025-11-12)
- Exact token distribution for classification vs summarization workloads (Owner: Mei to provide sample logs / token histogram by 2025-11-13)
- Legal: are ephemeral logs acceptable versus persistent recordings for 1 year? (Owner: Javier to loop in legal by 2025-11-14)

Immediate action items / next steps:
- RW: share SBOM and image signing docs (Leah) — due 2025-11-08.
- Praxis: provide sample request traces + anonymized payloads (Mei) — due 2025-11-13.
- RW SE (Omar): propose two initial perf configs: (A) low-latency classification profile (single model, int8, 8-GPU pool), (B) mixed profile (classification+batch summarization) including expected cost delta. Draft by 2025-11-11.
- Joint POC kickoff: tentatively week of 2025-11-18. Need to lock scope (classification-only vs full pipeline).

Notes to self (Leah):
- Emphasize prefix cache savings in follow-up — Praxis lives on repeatable short utterances across customers.
- Flag MTU/streaming issue to runtime team: confirm we respect TCP MSS and have non-blocking streaming fallback.
- Prepare short confluence page with architecture diagrams for both hybrid and air-gapped flows (link to add under linked_artifacts).

Quick risks / mitigation summary (to include in POC brief):
- Risk: networking prevents control plane connectivity -> Mitigation: air-gapped bundle or deploy control plane into Praxis VPC.
- Risk: burst QPS overwhelms single scaling policy -> Mitigation: warm pools + fast pre-warming + static reserved capacity for predicted peak windows.
- Risk: image policy friction -> Mitigation: provide signed image artifacts + SBOM + remote attestation options.

Final quick comments from Praxis:
- They want to see a 2-week POC that demonstrates classification latency and caching benefit on anonymized traces.
- Legal is strict on data residency; any hosted demo needs clear legal sign-off.

END NOTES
